floor_history.headline: recon: retired body 65 -> recovered WIP score-8 form transfers at 7 on soft-float -> int-typed stride+base sum gives 6; last 6 = sched1 LUID tie between the a2-site init and the call arg loads, proven
Floor holds at 6 (176/176, RA byte-identical to target); 16 structural spellings measured, both banked frontier routes F1 and F2 retired with mechanism cites, residual is a pure 3-insn emission-order

Judge-FAILed nv/nw body retired from candidate.c; measured that every source-level hoist of the a2 base costs a tenth callee-saved seat (+2 insns) and is not target-shaped; the s3 reg_n_sets mechanism

frontier.hypothesis: Some pass deletes the early `nv = (s32)r4 - K` insn and re-materializes `addiu a2,s4,-K` after the call's arg loads in the FAILed g17/g23 bodies; naming that pass names the only known mechanism that satisfies the sched1 LUID condition, and an ORDINARY-C construct may trigger the same transformation on the accumulator itself.
frontier.mechanism: Candidates are cse.c re-materialization at the copy `a2_offset = nv;`, combine.c folding the copy into the arithmetic at the copy site, or flow.c deleting the now-dead early set. Whichever it is, the insn is re-emitted with an INSN_LUID above the arg loads, which is what sched.c:2464's tie-break at the clock-64 pick reads - and what tools/gcc-2.7.2/expr.c:8641 / calls.c:1909 were read as forbidding (H7).
frontier.next_probe: pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8005D554 with tmp/grind/func_8005D554/s3/g17_perhalf_base.c applied, then again with s3/k1_perhalf_acc_hoist.c applied; diff the .cse, .combine and .flow dumps around the a2 base insn to identify the transformation, then search for a real, program-motivated copy (not an invented carrier) that reproduces it.

frontier.hypothesis: The sched1 clock-64 tie can be flipped from the PRIORITY side rather than the LUID side: lower the a2 init's INSN_PRIORITY (shorten its path to the block end) or raise the a0/a1 arg loads'.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c:2464 reaches the INSN_LUID tie-break only when priority and class are equal; every session so far has attacked the LUID term and none has attacked the priority term.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/sched_solver extract.py text1b + simulate.py --func func_8005D554 --pass 1 on the reset candidate.c and enumerate, in the exact model, which priority perturbation on uids 211 (a2 init), 240 (a0 load) and 242 (a1 load) flips the clock-64 pick; only then look for a C spelling that produces it at 176 instructions.

frontier.hypothesis: A fourth permuter seed - a chassis built by STACKING the s2 neutral spellings (z3 guard-duplicated while + x2 per-half blocks + v6 declaration order + w5 store order), all of which score 6 at 176 - sits one edit from the goal with a different emission order, unlike the 178-instruction g7 chassis that did not yield.
frontier.mechanism: The permuter yields from basins whose base score is near the target (z3 started at 310 and found 160); g7 started at 940 and stalled at 655. A stacked-neutral 176/6 chassis starts in the 310 class but with a different setup-block order than either spent seed.
frontier.next_probe: Build tmp/perm_5d554_stack from the stacked-neutral body, launch with tools/permuter_campaign.py -j 8, wait in-turn, and vet every find hard: this function's permuter attractor is the banned fresh multi-write carrier, and a find that spells one is not a candidate.

judge_constraints: No fresh (invented) local may be written more than once to act as a staging carrier for the a2-site base `(s32)r4 - K` or for any other value in this function, under any name; the existing-local borrow quadrant (staged-value-reused-variable, all six bounds) and the alternate-chassis route (frontier item 2, e.g. the z3 guard-duplicated while) remain open.
